explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/34: is S(π) = o(n²) for all π ∈ S_n, where S(π) counts distinct sums over consecutive positions? The page records the answer as no (Hegyvári; Konieczny). The statement negates the uniform form: for every c > 0, for all large n, every permutation has S(π) < c·n². `consecutiveSums` shifts values to 1,…,n via p k + 1 and forms the sums for u ≤ v. Uniformity over permutations is the only meaningful reading for a family varying with n. Faithful.
